headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared filesystem and file-parsing defaults; no direct evidence of stronger pairwise coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem, while the course agent reads and writes files and exposes agentic APIs. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let AutoGPT-supplied content be treated as instructions by the course agent. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or notebook workspace, injection becomes plausible.
IF the course agent parses AutoGPT-generated files as instructions or prompts, the attack path is active.
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of files produced by the other agent.
Add a manual review step before any prompt or notebook is consumed.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access with allowlisted egress; the course agent explicitly touches configuration secrets and research data classes. If they share a workspace, either agent can expose files the other can read or transmit. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or mounted volume, leakage is possible.
IF the course agent loads .env or notebook artifacts created by AutoGPT, secrets may be exposed.
mitigations: Keep secrets in a separate vault from shared workspaces.
Mount shared folders read-only where possible.
Remove secrets from any files exchanged between agents.
Rotate exposed API keys after any shared-run test.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell and spawn subprocesses, and AutoGPT can write the filesystem while the course agent can also write the filesystem. That creates overlapping mutable access even though AutoGPT does not advertise git writes. Without locking or isolation, concurrent edits can clobber files in a shared directory.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF either agent writes generated artifacts while the other is running, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Use file locks for any shared writes.
Snapshot the workspace before each run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The course agent exposes agentic ask/stream APIs and a LangGraph subagent model, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable context. AutoGPT can generate shell-driven artifacts that the course agent could ingest. No evidence shows automatic blind trust, but the default interaction path is still a plausible error cascade.
conditions: IF AutoGPT outputs are fed into the course agent without verification, errors can cascade.
IF the course agent uses AutoGPT-produced text as ground truth for downstream actions, impact expands.
mitigations: Require source verification before downstream use.
Insert a human approval step for any action derived from AutoGPT output.
Keep AutoGPT outputs in a draft-only folder.
Log provenance for every imported artifact.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: The course agent explicitly handles configuration secrets and research data, while AutoGPT has shell and filesystem access that could move those materials outside intended controls. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so the compliance concern is a generic retention/exposure mismatch rather than a proven regulatory breach.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workspace, compliance obligations apply.
IF logs or notebooks containing secrets are retained beyond policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared runs.
Purge logs and notebooks after testing.
Store secrets outside the workspace.
Document retention rules for both agents.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and certification controls.
